decision_semantics.FS: CONTINUE is required: early fails and depth10 succeeds
decision_semantics.SS: STOP is safe: both early and depth10 succeed
decision_semantics.SF: STOP is beneficial: early succeeds and depth10 rolls back
decision_semantics.FF: STOP is quality-neutral and cheaper: both fail

axes.unnecessary_continue_rate: P(CONTINUE | SS or SF or FF)

decision_semantics.why_not_plain_tpr_fpr: Early-sufficiency labels treat FF as negative, although stopping on FF is quality-neutral and saves compute. They also hide rollback-preserving SF states. The deployment action is rescue necessity, not absolute sufficiency.

gate.realistic_region_definition: minimum rescue recall <= 0.90 at unnecessary-continue rate >= 0.01
gate.judge_cost_note: The grid excludes auxiliary-judge cost. The reported budget at the 0.98 cap is the maximum equivalent Target-token allowance before the point ceases to pass deployment compute.

limitations: Design-exposed 256-query C1 cohort. Expected metrics assume a judge with class-conditional rates shared across decisions and independent decisions for expected Complete. A learned judge still requires query-grouped OOF and explicit compute accounting; this audit cannot establish learnability.
